summary: Reading School District opposes sunset or limits on E‑Rate, supports keeping poverty‑based discounts, and wants to preserve local control over screen‑time and CIPA filtering. Reading School District supports preserving MIBS and dark fiber, opposes percentage‑based consultant fees, and backs expanding CIPA filtering obligations with eligibility, while taking no position on self‑provisioned construction. The Reading School District opposes FCC proposals to condition E‑Rate funding on screen‑time limits, parental opt‑outs, and network‑level filtering of third‑party devices, arguing that such measures would disproportionately burden disadvantaged students and impose undue administrative costs. Reading School District argues that MIBS should remain eligible regardless of district size, that documentation requirements for MIBS are burdensome relative to the value of the service, that applicants should be able to compare MIBS bids with internal connection bids, and that pre‑kindergarten students should not be cost‑allocated or excluded from funding requests.
